title: Inquest ordered in police shooting death of Burlington driver
article: An inquest will be held into the shooting death of a man on the streets of Burlington by a police officer.
The regional coroner has set Jan. 15 as the start date for an inquest into the killing of a 34-year-old Burlington man, shot during a confrontation with Halton Regional Police.
The announcement also marked the first time the victim, Carl Kim, has been publicly identified. Kim, 34, died on Saturday, March 12, 2011 at Joseph Brant Hospital.

Both Halton police and the province's Special Investigations Unit refused to release the man's name at the time of the shooting and after the subsequent SIU decision not to lay charges against the officer who shot Kim.
The incident began when Halton police received several calls about an erratic driver. An officer tracked a car and after a short pursuit stopped the vehicle around 7:30 p.m.

The driver got out of the car and an altercation occurred. The officer had his Kevlar vest pulled off and baton knocked away before using his gun, the SIU said. The man picked up the police baton and charged at the officer, who then fired the fatal shot.

Dr. Roger Skinner, Regional Supervising Coroner for the Central Region, Toronto West Office, said in in a press release that the inquest is expected to last three days and will hear from about 11 witnesses.
It will begin at 9:30 a.m. Jan. 15 in the main floor auditorium of a building at 5500 North Service Rd. in Burlington.
Dr. James Kovacs will be the presiding coroner.
Inquests in Ontario examine the events surrounding deaths like Kim's, with a jury having the power to make recommendations aimed at preventing similar ones.
